questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests time-window dynamic data with multi-key aggregates and top-k queries, challenging both data layout and lazy deletions.

## Key Concepts
- Time-window maintenance with insertions and deletions
- Per-user aggregate tracking for top-k queries
- Per-service latency distribution for kth-largest queries

## Code Example
```javascript
class LogStore {
  insertLog(userId, serviceId, timestamp, latency) {
    // Add to global treap by timestamp; update per-user and per-service structures
  }
  eraseLogsInTimeWindow(start, end) {
    // Mark logs in [start, end] as deleted; adjust aggregates lazily
  }
}
```

## Data Structures
- **Global treap**: Time-ordered logs for window queries
- **Per-user trees**: Track total latency by user for top-k
- **Per-service trees**: Maintain latency distribution for kth-largest
- **Lazy deletion**: Mark invalid entries, clean during queries

## Update Rules
- Insert: Update all structures in O(log n)
- Delete: Mark as deleted, defer cleanup
- Query: Verify consistency, trigger cleanup if needed

## Edge Cases
- Duplicate timestamps: Use secondary key (userId, serviceId)
- Empty windows: Return empty results
- Large deletions: Batch cleanup to maintain performance

## Code Example

```javascript
class Fenwick {
  constructor(n){ this.n=n; this.bit=new Array(n+1).fill(0); }
  update(i, delta){ for(; i<=this.n; i+= i&-i) this.bit[i]+=delta; }
  query(i){ let s=0; for(; i>0; i-= i&-i) s+=this.bit[i]; return s; }
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Replicates real-world autocomplete ranking: vocab grows/shrinks and weights reflect relevance. A Trie with per-node weight multisets enables fast prefix-based sums and order statistics while handling duplicates.

## Key Concepts

**Data Structure Choice: Balanced BST or Ordered Map**
Each Trie node stores a Map<weight, count> sorted by weight. This enables:
- O(log M) kthLargest via binary search on sorted keys, where M = distinct weights at node
- O(1) sum via precomputed subtreeTotal
- O(1) insert/erase per node with count management

**Why not O(depth) naive merge?**
Merging all descendant weights at query time would be O(depth × branching). By maintaining aggregates at each node, we achieve O(1) sum and O(M log M) kthLargest where M = distinct weights (typically small).

**Erase Boundary Cases Handled:**
- Weight not found in multiset → return false, no change
- Count reaches 0 → delete key to keep map minimal
- Negative counts prevented by count check before decrement

## Time Complexity

| Operation | Time | Space |
|-----------|------|-------|
| insertWord | O(wordLen) | O(wordLen) new nodes |
| eraseWord | O(wordLen) | O(1) | 
| sumWeightsWithPrefix | O(prefixLen) | O(1) |
| kthLargestWeightWithPrefix | O(M log M) | O(1) |

## Usage Example

```javascript
const dict = new DynamicPrefixDictionary();
dict.insertWord("cat", 10);
dict.insertWord("car", 20);
dict.insertWord("card", 5);
dict.sumWeightsWithPrefix("car");    // 25 (20 + 5)
dict.kthLargestWeightWithPrefix("car", 1); // 20
dict.kthLargestWeightWithPrefix("car", 2); // 5
dict.eraseWord("car", 20);
dict.sumWeightsWithPrefix("car");    // 5
```
